title: Time, from my Raspberry Pi.
intro: I built a Stratum 1 time server at home. These clocks use its GPS/PPS time when connected, displayed in your timezone, mine, and UTC.
deviceOffset: Estimated correction to your device clock
refreshValue: Every 60 seconds while this tab is visible
offsetNote: A positive correction means the Pi clock was ahead of your device at synchronization. This is an estimate, limited by network delay.
sourceBody: My Raspberry Pi gets time from a GPS receiver and its pulse-per-second signal. It also serves NTP to my home network. This page reads that same disciplined system clock through a small time API.

steps.title: GPS → Raspberry Pi
steps.body: GPS and PPS discipline the Pi clock. The API checks that PPS is selected, Stratum 1 is reported, and synchronization is healthy.

steps.title: Pi → Cloudflare
steps.body: A protected tunnel carries fresh timestamps to the website. The browser never receives the service credentials.

steps.title: Cloudflare → Your browser
steps.body: Three samples estimate the time correction. The browser advances that clock locally between synchronizations.

accuracyBody: I subtract the Pi's processing time from the round trip and estimate the return journey as half the remaining delay. Unequal travel times still introduce error.
fallbackBody: If the request fails, times out, or reports an unhealthy clock, every display immediately uses Your Device Clock (Fallback). Your timezone comes from your browser settings; it does not decide the synchronized time.
dashboardTitle: A little closer to on time.
meterNote: Device minus GPS time. Shaded band: ± half the network round trip, an estimate rather than guaranteed accuracy.
satelliteNote: Receiver counts refresh with clock synchronization. Individual satellite observations stay private.
dashboardIntro: A GPS receiver, one pulse per second, and a Raspberry Pi keeping its clock in check. These are the live measurements behind the time.
referenceNote: The Pi’s disciplined system time, advanced in your browser between syncs. Network delay limits how accurately it arrives here.
receptionNote: Used counts satellites in the receiver solution. Signals received counts satellites with a reported signal above zero. These bars show totals, not individual satellites.
tdopNote: How satellite geometry affects the time solution. This is a dimensionless factor, not a clock error or an accuracy guarantee.
systemOffsetSecondsHelp: Pi system clock minus chrony’s NTP clock.
lastOffsetSecondsHelp: Estimated local offset at the last clock update.
rmsOffsetSecondsHelp: Longer term measure of offset variation.
frequencyPpmHelp: Estimated free-running error. Positive means fast.
skewPpmHelp: Estimated error bound on the frequency.
rootDispersionSecondsHelp: Accumulated timing uncertainty to the reference.
residualFrequencyPpmHelp: Difference still left in the frequency estimate.
rootDelaySecondsHelp: Total path delay to the primary reference.
updateIntervalSecondsHelp: Time between chrony’s two latest clock updates.
disciplineNote: These are chrony’s own control-loop estimates, not an independent measurement of absolute UTC accuracy. They are separate from the browser’s network estimate below. 1 ppm is 1 microsecond per second.
lockNote: Observed lock starts when this service sees PPS selected, resets on a failed check or service restart, and is checked every 10 seconds.
privacyNote: Only aggregate receiver data and clock measurements are public. Coordinates, satellite identities, and sky positions stay private.
traceAccessible: Chrony’s last clock offset over samples collected during this visit. Numeric samples are available below.
traceWaiting: Collecting samples. The trace appears after the next synchronization.
traceNote: One chrony offset per browser synchronization, up to 60 samples in this tab. Gaps are unobserved time. This is a snapshot of clock control, not historical uptime or absolute accuracy.
stabilitySubtitle: 13 weeks of recorded checks · UTC days
calendarHint: Select a day to inspect its lock percentage and monitoring coverage.
stabilityWaiting: Waiting for the first clock sample.
stabilityNote: Each square is one UTC day. Color shows the share of observed checks with PPS selected and a healthy Stratum 1 clock. Stripes mean less than 90% monitoring coverage; grey means no checks. Gaps are unknown, never assumed healthy. Stored on the Pi across restarts, with checks roughly every 10 seconds. This measures clock lock, not website uptime, and records from when monitoring was enabled.
historyNotLive: Showing the last received history. Live synchronization is unavailable.
